**Operator:** Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited Q4 and FY26 earning conference call hosted by MUFG InTime India Private Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Nikunj Jain from MUFG InTime India Private Limited. Thank you and over to you, sir.

**Nikunj Jain:** Thank you. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. I welcome you all to the Q4 and FY26 earnings conference call of Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited. Today on the call, we have from the management Mr. Hitesh Mehta, Whole-Time Director; Mr. Manmohan Sharma, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Neeraj Vinayak, Vice President, Investor Relations; and Mr. Rohit Wade, General Manager, Investor Relations. Before we proceed with this call, I would like to mention that some of the statements made in today's call may be forward-looking in nature and may involve risks and uncertainties. For more details, kindly refer to the investor presentation and other filings that can be found on the company's website. Without further ado, I would like to hand over the call to Mr. Manmohan Sharma for his opening remarks and then we will open the floor for Q&A. Thank you and over to you, sir.

**Manmohan Sharma:** Thank you, Nikunj. Good afternoon, everyone. And I would like to extend a warm welcome to all participants for joining the earnings conference call of Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited for discussing our business performance for Q4 and FY2026. I hope you all had an opportunity to review our financial results and investor presentation which have been made available on the stock exchanges and are uploaded on company's website.

I would like to commence by showing my sincere gratitude to all our stakeholders for their unwavering trust and support. Your continued confidence in our vision and execution has played an important role in shaping our journey so far. Today on the call, I have along with me, the key members of our management team. Starting with our financial results for the quarter, our revenue from operations stood at ₹1,102.40 crores, reflecting a growth of 131.31% compared to the same quarter of last year. EBITDA comes at ₹206.82 crores with a margin of 18.76%. PAT for the quarter reached at ₹155.72 crores, marking a year-on-year increase of 66.08%.

For the financial year 2026, we reported revenue of ₹3,331.42 crores, a growth of 108.51% over FY2025. EBITDA stood at ₹641.10 crores, up 106.21% year-on-year basis. While PAT reached at ₹478.65 crores, showing growth of 109.09% on year-on-year basis. These results highlight our strong execution capability and the operating leverage that we continue to build across our business.

From an operational standpoint, FY2026 was a year marked by scale and steady execution. During FY2026, we have successfully executed 2,727 megawatt peak of projects, which is highest for any year. This reflects the depth of our execution capability for the year end, our unexecuted order book stood at 2.83 gigawatt peak, providing us with a strong visibility and continuity of business going forward. At the same time, our O&M portfolio stood at 1.18 gigawatt peak, further strengthening our base of recurring revenue and reinforcing our role as a reliable long-term partner for our customers. Overall, this performance demonstrates our ability to grow responsibly while maintaining consistency and reliability across project execution.

Let me now turn to the broader industry environment where momentum across India's renewable energy sector remains strong. The country's clean energy transition continued to accelerate with total installed renewable capacity now crossing 274 gigawatt and solar alone contributing over 150 gigawatt as of March 2026. The growth is due to rapid expansion with contribution from ground-mounted solar plants of 114.87 gigawatt, grid-connected solar rooftop of 25.73 gigawatt and other solar segments contributing to 9.66 gigawatt. This shift demonstrates the growing importance of solar within India's energy ecosystem. In FY2026, over 44 gigawatt of solar capacity was added, representing a substantial increase from 23.83 gigawatt in the previous year.

In FY2026, solar emerged as the leading driver of capacity additions, accounting for approximately 82% of total renewable installations, reinforcing its position as a primary growth driver within the sector. India's renewable energy growth continued to be supported by stable policies framework such as the National Solar Mission, PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar Yojana alongside expanding demand across utility scale, rooftop and decentralized segment, which is improving visibility for EPC player. Additionally, battery energy storage system (BESS) are now emerging as a key enabler for grid stability with increasing inclusion of renewable tenders, opening up new opportunity within the EPC ecosystem.

In this environment, we are well positioned with a strong order book, a healthy O&M portfolio and expanding into BESS EPC while maintaining our focus on execution discipline and operational efficiency. We are encouraged by the progress made in FY2026 and are hopeful about the opportunities ahead. Waaree Renewable Technology is committed to driving sustainable growth and creating lasting value for all stakeholders. Thank you once again for your continued support. We now open the floor for any questions you may have.

**Nikunj Jain:** Thank you so much, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question and answer session. Anyone who wishes to ask a question may press star and one on their touchtone telephone. If you wish to remove yourself from the question queue, you may press star and two. Participants are requested to use handsets while asking a question. Ladies and gentlemen, we'll wait for a moment while the question queue assembles.

## Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited Q4 and FY26 Earnings Call Summary

### 1. TL;DR:
Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited reported strong Q4 and FY26 financial results, driven by robust execution in the Indian renewable energy sector, particularly solar EPC projects. The company achieved significant revenue and PAT growth, maintained a healthy order book, and is strategically expanding into Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and IPP projects for recurring revenue.

### 2. Key Themes:
*   **Strong Financial Performance:** Significant year-on-year growth in revenue and PAT for both Q4 and FY26, demonstrating strong execution capabilities and operational leverage.
*   **Robust Order Book & Execution:** Achieved highest-ever project execution of 2.727 GWp in FY26, with an unexecuted order book of 2.83 GWp providing strong business visibility.
*   **Strategic Expansion:** Focus on expanding into Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) EPC and developing smaller-scale Independent Power Producer (IPP) projects to diversify revenue streams and build recurring income.
*   **Stable Industry Environment:** India's renewable energy sector continues to accelerate, supported by stable policy frameworks and increasing demand across various solar segments, with solar being the primary growth driver.
*   **Margin Management:** While Q4 EBITDA margins were 18.76%, the full-year FY26 EBITDA margin was over 19.24%, with management targeting around 15% as a threshold, but continuously striving for operational improvements.

### 3. Action Items/Next Steps:
*   **FY27 Execution:** The existing 2.83 GWp order book is expected to be executed over the next 12-15 months, supplemented by new orders.
*   **IPP Project Commissioning:** Additional 227 MWp IPP projects currently under construction are expected to be commissioned during the current financial year (FY27).
*   **BESS Project Execution:** One relatively smaller BESS project is currently being executed and is expected to be completed in the current financial year, with more inquiries anticipated.
*   **Order Pipeline Conversion:** Actively chasing an order pipeline of approximately 36 GW (23 GW domestic, 12 GW international), with expectations of converting some into firm orders in coming quarters.

### 4. Technical Glossary:
*   **Q4:** Fourth quarter of the financial year.
*   **FY26:** Financial Year 2025-2026.
*   **EBITDA:** Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization – a measure of a company's operating performance.
*   **PAT:** Profit After Tax – the net profit of a company after all expenses, including taxes, have been deducted.
*   **GWp (Gigawatt peak):** A unit of power for solar installations, representing the maximum power output under ideal conditions.
*   **MWp (Megawatt peak):** A unit of power for solar installations, 1/1000th of a GWp.
*   **O&M (Operations & Maintenance):** Services provided to ensure the continued efficient operation of power plants.
*   **EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction):** A form of contracting agreement where the contractor is responsible for all activities from design to commissioning.
*   **IPP (Independent Power Producer):** A non-utility entity that owns and operates facilities to generate electricity for sale to utilities or end-users.
*   **BESS (Battery Energy Storage System):** Systems that store electrical energy from renewable sources for later use, crucial for grid stability.
*   **PM KUSUM:** Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan – a scheme for farmers to install solar pumps and grid-connected solar power plants.
*   **PM Surya Ghar Yojana:** A government scheme promoting rooftop solar installations.
*   **ALCM (Approved List of Models and Manufacturers):** Regulations in India for solar module manufacturing and procurement.
*   **DCR (Domestic Content Requirement):** A policy requiring a certain percentage of components in a project to be sourced domestically.
*   **BOS (Balance of System):** All components of a photovoltaic system other than the solar panels themselves.
*   **CERC (Central Electricity Regulatory Commission):** The regulatory body for the power sector in India.
*   **IRR (Internal Rate of Return):** A metric used in capital budgeting to estimate the profitability of potential investments.
*   **CWIP (Capital Work-in-Progress):** The cost of fixed assets that are currently under construction and not yet ready for use.
*   **OCF (Operating Cash Flow):** The cash generated by a company's normal business operations.

### 5. Signals for Research:
*   **Bullish points:**
    *   Strong financial growth (revenue +131.31% Q4 YoY, +108.51% FY26 YoY; PAT +66.08% Q4 YoY, +109.09% FY26 YoY).
    *   Highest-ever project execution (2.727 GWp) in FY26.
    *   Healthy unexecuted order book (2.83 GWp) providing strong revenue visibility.
    *   Expanding O&M portfolio (1.18 GWp) for recurring revenue.
    *   Strategic entry into BESS EPC, aligning with growing industry demand for grid stability.
    *   Government push for renewable energy (National Solar Mission, PM KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar Yojana) provides a supportive policy framework.
    *   Ability to pass through module price increases to customers, mitigating ALCM impact.
    *   Majority of receivables are less than six months and secured by LCs, indicating good working capital management.
*   **Risks/cautions:**
    *   Quarterly revenue realization can be volatile depending on the mix of projects (with/without modules).
    *   Order inflow saw a slight decrease (5%) in FY26 compared to FY25, though management expects conversion from a large pipeline.
    *   Potential for increased competition impacting margins, though management maintains a 15% EBITDA threshold.
    *   Land acquisition challenges for ground-mounted solar projects, though currently managed by developers.
    *   Slowdown in tendering activity in FY26 compared to FY25.
*   **Watch items:**
    *   Conversion rate of the 36 GW order pipeline (23 GW domestic, 12 GW international).
    *   Impact of BESS projects on revenue and margins as this segment opens up.
    *   Commissioning timeline and financial contribution of the 227 MWp IPP projects.
    *   Any potential impact of CERC orders regarding RE evacuation infrastructure in key states like Rajasthan.
    *   Cash conversion ratio and OCF generation in future periods, given the slight drop in FY26.
    *   Breakdown of module procurement from parent company (Waaree Energies) versus third-party vendors.
